idiom_name: dyn Trait trait objects (Box<dyn T> / &dyn T) + std::any::Any
implementation_notes: A trait object is the language's built-in erasure: a pointer (Box<dyn Draw>, &dyn Draw, Arc<dyn Draw>) pairs the concrete value with a vtable, so a Vec<Box<dyn Draw>> holds unrelated types that implement Draw, from any crate, without sharing a base. The trait is the concept, an impl block is the model, and the coercion at the binding site is explicit; dyn-compatibility rules state what may be erased (no generic methods, no Self by value, one non-auto trait). When the concrete type must be recovered, std::any::Any plus downcast_ref provides the fully erased, type-tested form - Box<dyn Error> is the ubiquitous standard-library instance. For a closed set of types an enum with match is the idiomatic static alternative and avoids both the vtable and the allocation.
pitfalls: Trait objects are dynamically sized and must live behind a pointer, and every call is indirect (no inlining or specialization) - keep impl Trait and generics for hot, statically known paths.
dyn-compatibility limits what is callable: generic methods, methods returning Self and by-value self cannot be used through dyn, so mark statically-only parts where Self: Sized.
Any tests concrete types only (not trait implementation) and requires 'static; calling .type_id() on a Box<dyn Any> returns the Box's TypeId, so dereference first: (&*boxed).type_id().
